html:
An Islamic revival movement founded in 1889 at Qadian in the Punjab by Mirza Ghulam Ahmad, who claimed to be the promised Messiah and Mahdi expected at the end of times.

He taught a peaceful jihad of the pen rather than the sword, and argued against both Christian missionaries and the Hindu reformers of the Arya Samaj, who were active in the Punjab at the time. The movement built a strong organisation of missions, schools and publications.

After his death it split in 1914. The larger branch is led by a line of caliphs; a smaller Lahore group sees him as a reformer, not a prophet. Mainstream Muslims reject the claim that any prophet can come after Muhammad, and that is the core of the conflict.

At Partition the main community moved from Qadian, which fell in India, to Rabwah in Pakistan. In 1974 Pakistan's constitution declared Ahmadis non-Muslims, and a 1984 law made it a crime for them to call themselves Muslim; the caliph moved to London. Ahmadis face persecution in Pakistan still. The physicist Abdus Salam was a member. Today the community has millions of followers in many countries.
sum: An Islamic revival movement founded in 1889 at Qadian in the Punjab by Mirza Ghulam Ahmad, who claimed to be the promised Messiah and Mahdi expected at the end of times.
